Five vertical bars are shown, each with a percentage label centered above it. Bar heights increase left-to-right to the second bar, then decrease, with the second bar (Groundwater) being the tallest.

public_definitions: User goal: 'Review the urban water-supply dashboard, identify the largest urban water-supply contribution source, then route that source record to escalated contribution review.'
Routing criterion (readonly field): 'Largest urban water-supply contribution source'.
Option 1: 'Route Surface water to escalated contribution review'.
Option 2: 'Route Groundwater to escalated contribution review'.
Option 3: 'Keep Desalination in routine source monitoring'.
uncertain: The printed numeric annotations (e.g., '41.2%' for Surface water, '29.8%' for Groundwater) do not match the visual bar heights on the y-axis (Surface water bar reaches ~41, Groundwater bar reaches ~68). It is unclear whether the labels or the bar heights represent the true 'contribution' values.

The task asks for the 'largest urban water-supply contribution source'. Based on bar height, Groundwater is largest. Based on printed labels, Surface water (41.2%) is largest. This conflict is unresolved from the image alone.
